item.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted ballistic missile fired towards southern Saudi town
item.description:
Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted ballistic missile fired towards southern Saudi town

The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Saturday it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired by the Iran-aligned group towards the Saudi town of Al Shuqaiq, adding that the debris came down without causing any civilian casualties.

Al Shuqaiq, on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast in Jazan province, is home to major desalination and power generation facilities supplying water and electricity to the kingdom's southern regions.

Reporting by Reuters

item.title: Argentina fails to block oil drilling off Falkland Islands
item.description:
UK government calls on Buenos Aires to end ‘economic pressure’ on islands after international tribunal’s ruling

The UK has called on Argentina to stop its economic warfare on the Falkland islands after Buenos Aires failed in a legal attempt to terminate an offshore oil project vital to the future of the British overseas territory.

An application by the South American country for suspension of the Sea Lion project was rejected on Saturday by the international tribunal for the law of the seas (Itlos) on the grounds that the issue lay outside its jurisdiction.

item.title: Armed group boards cargo ship off Yemen and takes control, UKMTO says
item.description:
Armed group boards cargo ship off Yemen and takes control, UKMTO says

Armed individuals boarded a cargo ship 64 nautical miles southwest of Yemen's Balhaf at 0630 GMT and took control of the vessel, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said on Saturday, citing the ship's master.

UKMTO said authorities had been informed and advised vessels in the area to proceed with caution.

A European Union naval mission also reported a piracy incident in the area on Saturday, but it was not immediately clear if it was the same ship whose attack was reported by UKMTO.

Reporting by Reuters

item.title: Iran official: Iraq must not become a 'tool' of Trump
item.description:
Iran official: Iraq must not become a 'tool' of Trump

Mohammad Mokhber, an ​adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, warned Iraq in a post on X on Saturday that it must not become a "tool of Trump" after media reports that Iraq had closed several crossings following US efforts to blockade Iran's land borders.

“This unbreakable bond [with Iran] requires Baghdad to remain vigilant on the issue of borders so that it does not become a tool of the enemies of Islam or give in to the policies of the criminal Trump,” Mokhber said.

item.title: Drones ‘swarmed’ US army base at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk in November
item.description:
Personnel told to take cover after ‘suspected unauthorised activity’ of six drones that were repelled but not recovered

Drones reportedly swarmed a US army base in Suffolk earlier this month and were not recovered after being repelled.

Personnel at RAF Lakenheath were told to take cover on 13 November after “suspected unauthorised drone activity”. The US air force confirmed the so-called Charlie alert at the time, the second-highest threat level, but released few details. Sirens could be heard at the base. Iran is suspected of being involved.

item.title: Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production
item.description:
Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production

Iran has repaired three gas pipelines damaged in the early weeks of the US-Israeli war, returning them to production at the South Pars gas field, the country’s state-run Mehr news agency said.

The agency said that lines 1 and 4 of the fourth refinery and line 3 of the sixth refinery were back in operation, adding 20 million cubic metres of gas a day to Iran's gas output capacity.

President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the development, saying: “Getting through the winter without cutting off electricity, gas, and fuel needed for production requires the support of the people, the efforts of producers, and improving infrastructure.”

War damage to Iran’s energy infrastructure has compounded energy shortages. As winter draws close, authorities have announced two-hour electricity cuts in parts of the country.

item.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway

Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.
